items.summary: Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-76519, an arbitrary file write in the Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation) path of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets an unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through the device write files and run commands as root (CVSS 9.8); Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of exploitation in October 2026, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. items.headline: nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update to 1.31.10, 1.30.8, Plus 37.3.1.1
items.summary: F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007. The memory-corruption fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, nginx 1.31.10, 1.30.8 and NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 add a fix for one CPU-exhaustion flaw, and NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update. Rapid7 published a proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007, CERT-EU reports no exploitation, and NCSC.ch, CERT-EU, CERT.at and NCSC-NL issued warnings; Unit 42 reached pre-authentication code execution through CVE-2026-123633 as the worker user in a lab, on a non-default configuration and with a separate memory leak that F5 has not given a CVE. Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled as affected, Veeam lists its 13.1 Software and Infrastructure Appliances (fixed through Veeam Updater), Cisco lists Catalyst Center, Identity Services Engine 3.5, Nexus 3000 and 9000 in standalone NX-OS mode, UCS Director and about 20 other products with fixes dated November 2026 to March 2027 or still to be determined, Siemens and Synology list products with fixes pending or none, and Fortinet confirms FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiMail, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiADC, FortiWeb and FortiSIEM not impacted while 29 product names, FortiAuthenticator among them, remain under investigation.

items.headline: GeoServer RCE chain: public PoC, CISA lists two flaws as exploited; update to 3.0.2, 2.28.6 or 2.27.7
items.summary: The GeoServer project published a batch of security advisories on 2026-11-23, most for flaws fixed in 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7, and five of them chain an anonymous WFS request to code execution: a path disclosure, a service-security bypass with a prefixed service name, an XML injection, a predictable remember-me key that forges an administrator session (critical, CVSS 4.0 9.2) and a JDBC deserialization. The reporter, who says it works on a default installation, published a full-chain proof of concept the same day; the project announced the fixed releases on 2026-10-19. CISA added CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-27 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe, watchTowr reports exploitation attempts in the form of error-based probes that create and invoke stored queries, and NCSC Switzerland rates the chain actively exploited.

actions: Patch CVE-2026-46300 on every Linux host that runs PHP or other internet-facing code, then on multi-tenant hosts, container nodes and CI runners: apply the distribution kernel update and reboot; until then, where IPsec is not in use, block and unload the `esp4`, `esp6` and `rxrpc` modules (this breaks IPsec), and drop the page cache so a file already modified in memory reloads from disk.

On any PHP web host, appliance or management server that was reachable and unpatched for the PHP2Shell flaws, look for PHP files in web-reachable directories that nobody deployed, an outbound SSH session from the host that a systemd service or an rc.local entry keeps up, and password-spray bursts against Active Directory from the host's address, because Dream Research reports a chain of the two flaws that did exactly that.
items.headline: CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia): CISA lists the Linux kernel root flaw as exploited, chained with PHP2Shell
items.summary: CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia", CVSS 7.8) is a local privilege escalation in the Linux kernel's xfrm ESP-in-TCP path, one of three CVEs Red Hat groups as "Dirty Frag"; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, and Dream Research reports such a chain against 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and a US government-affiliated network. Its public exploit overwrites /usr/bin/su in the page cache, and Red Hat confirms RHEL kernels are affected (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28 · Dream Research, 2026-10-29 · Red Hat RHSB-2026-003).

items.summary: The Ruby project released 4.0.10, 3.4.13 and 3.3.14 on 2026-11-18 for seven memory-corruption flaws in the regexp engine and in string case conversion, three rated Critical, and says it knows of proofs of concept that reach remote code execution. items.summary: DIVD, the Dutch vulnerability-disclosure CSIRT, says attackers entered its network on 2026-09-21 through two Zammad flaws it calls previously unknown: CVE-2026-102489, a session hijack leading to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0 to 6.5.4, and CVE-2026-102490, a local escalation from that user to root. Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations, Zammad 7.2.3 of 2026-11-11, a critical security update, supersedes it, and 6.5.5 (2026-10-15) is an emergency fix for the code-execution flaw in the otherwise unsupported 6.5 series; 7.2.1 (2026-10-06) had fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited. DIVD's forensic report of 2026-11-25 says the attacker likely used ARTEX and moved from the Zammad host to Jira and Confluence by ARP poisoning and forged administrator session tokens.

items.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory, first published on 2026-10-21 and revised since, says active exploitation has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, and Dream Research, with Unit 42's verification, reports a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw that rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea and went on to attack a US government-affiliated Active Directory. items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-103406 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25, after BSI revised its advisory to say the flaw is being exploited. items.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A hidden 'code-of-the-day' login is on CISA's exploited list; two post-auth flaws follow
items.summary: Companion disclosure to Claroty's Copeland research, same team and publish day. items.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE flaws, Strict mode does not remove them; France blames IRGC
items.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores, and on 2026-11-09 France's foreign ministry attributed that campaign, and only that campaign, to the Iranian unit Shahid Kaveh. More followed: more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops on 2026-11-02, altered cold-room settings at three sites of the French blood service through a supplier, and, per SRF on 2026-11-05, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores in Switzerland. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, and NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited. On 2026-11-11 Midnight Blue reported six pre-authentication remote-code-execution flaws in all Danfoss AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2, and on 2026-11-20 Danfoss published CVE-2026-129713 (CVSS 9.3, an unauthenticated stack overflow in AK-SM 8xxA firmware 5.4.0 and earlier, fix only in an announced 5.5.x) and CVE-2026-127057 (CVSS 9.9, default credentials on every legacy AK-SC 355 and AK-SM 800, no fix); CCB says updating, new passwords and Strict mode are insufficient, so removing internet exposure comes first, and BACS's statement of 2026-11-10 that updates fix the known flaws predates the report and does not cover the six. CISA added three older AK-SM 800A flaws (CVE-2023-25914, CVE-2023-25915 and CVE-2025-41450) to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 without tying them to this campaign.

items.headline: N-central: Hotfix 3 fixes 17 more CVEs and blocks the Legacy API; 4EverAble2Shell exploited; upgrade Agents too
items.summary: An independent researcher published proof-of-concept code on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 for what Huntress counts as 33 critical flaws in N-able's N-central appliance, and a second disclosure on 2026-11-12 added 4EverAble2Shell, a chain through Apache Axis (CVE-2026-90436) that works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is on and is exploited on at least 21 production servers, and Agent2Shell, SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints. Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26, 2026-11-10) fixed seven CVE ids and Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16) fixes 17 more, hardens how Agents and Probes authenticate and blocks the Legacy API permanently, but N-able does not name either chain or say it is fixed; Huntress reports public proof-of-concept code for all 17 and no exploitation of them in its partners' environments. Every on-premises server and every Agent and Probe must be on Hotfix 3, including those already on Hotfix 2.

actions: Update every ScreenConnect technician host client and Access agent to 26.6.5 or later now, not only the server, because the vulnerable code runs on the technician's machine; where that waits, remove the TransferFiles permission from every role and session group (Administration > Security > Roles).

Treat any pre-26.6.5 client that shows a second, unfamiliar RMM tool or an unexplained ScreenConnect connection ID as compromised and reimage it rather than patching in place, because every Host that joined a session with an infected client can have received and run the same infection chain.

On every ScreenConnect server, read a copy of App_Data\\Session.db for guest-originated RanFiles or SentFiles events that overlap an open host connection, and on any hit isolate the technician's workstation and rotate every credential reachable from it (RMM, PSA, vault, customer admin accounts), because Huntress saw one workstation fully compromised nine seconds after its client ran a guest-pushed file.

items.headline: ScreenConnect clients before 26.6.5 run guest-pushed files unprompted; Huntress confirms exploitation against MSPs

Huntress has confirmed exploitation against MSP technicians since October 2026, with attacker guests spraying run-file requests across 42 MSP servers. Earlier, from 20 August, Huntress saw rogue ScreenConnect clients that push their infection chain as an auto-run file transfer on every new connection, behaviour that matches the flaw, though Huntress does not tie those incidents to the CVE.

items.headline: Cisco Expressway root RCE is exploited (CISA KEV, F6 incident): upgrade clustered units to X15.5.20 and check them
items.summary: Cisco's disclosure of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 3.1 9.8), which lets an unauthenticated attacker who holds persistent cookies run operating-system commands as root on Expressway-C and Expressway-E configured in a cluster; X15.5.3 and earlier get X15.5.20, X14 and earlier must migrate, and there is no workaround. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, and F6 reports that, soon after a public proof of concept appeared, attackers compromised two internet-reachable X15.5.3 devices, reached two internal cluster nodes through one and ran Python scripts for scanning and credential theft, while Cisco's advisory still says it knows of no malicious use. The same-day hardening releases for the Unified CM family and Unity Connection (up to 9.8, fixed in 15SU5) and for Snort 3 (9.0) are not known to be exploited.

items.headline: TYPO3: backend user to installer to admin and RCE (SA-027 Critical); Form Framework flaw SA-029 exploited; update now
items.summary: TYPO3 published ten core advisories on 2026-11-17 for 10.0.0 to 14.3.11, fixed in 14.3.12 LTS, 13.4.40 LTS, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS. TYPO3 states that SA-029, a Medium information disclosure in the Form Framework that can become cross-site scripting through uploaded HTML, is known to be actively exploited, naming no actor or victim.

items.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
items.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating and has added the case to its criminal proceeding against Akira. Tamedia reports that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom, while PK Softech and the federal bodies say no concrete ransom demand reached them; Publica and several other funds say their insured persons' personal data has presumably left. Cantonal police warn that criminals could use leaked personal and financial data for investment-fraud calls.

VulnCheck's sensors recorded exploitation of an unauthenticated configuration write (CVE-2026-124014) from 2026-11-12 and root-command probes against CVE-2026-124010 from 2026-11-13, by opportunistic scanners it does not tie to the October refrigeration attacks. The injection flaws are fixed on the current firmware branch, while the password flaws reach the last firmware, 5.8.8, and stay unfixed because Copeland ended software support on 2026-03-16; Copeland tells operators to remove all XWEB EVO units from the public internet.

items.headline: FBI: various actors run ARTEX against many sectors, government included; Microsoft now names six users
items.summary: Microsoft reports that since at least September 2026 Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, has used ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework, to automate scanning, password spraying and OAuth-application abuse against hundreds of organizations across many industries including government, reaching privileged cloud access in under three hours in several cases; Expel saw the same infrastructure create its own accounts through Okta self-service registration. Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report on 2026-10-31 that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated in incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations, and that the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep it in circulation. CrowdStrike and Recorded Future document another actor using the framework, and Seoul police referred a criminal group's leader to prosecutors on 2026-10-23 for extorting 38 of more than 90 organizations, with the same framework according to BleepingComputer. Microsoft adds on 2026-11-06 another cluster, the Cambodia-based, financially motivated Storm-3358 targeting financial organisations, and Check Point reads ten exposed operator consoles that show near-autonomous, opportunistic ARTEX campaigns. CERT-EU says AI-driven activity against the EU institutions it protects highly likely involved ARTEX. The FBI's FLASH of 2026-11-13 says a variety of actors have used ARTEX since at least August against sectors including financial services, government, technology and defense, and lists the observed techniques, among them cloud-trust and vendor-credential pivots, Kudu abuse and Active Directory credential theft. Microsoft's defender guide of 2026-11-25 widens its named ARTEX users to six, adding the North Korean clusters Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet and the clusters Crystal Typhoon and Salt Typhoon, says ThreatBook now sells an ARTEX Pro, and lists detections on the web server, in identity logs and on egress. Wiz shows that ARTEX and Cairn write a numeric intent ID into names they create in victim environments, ARTEX's drawn from a per-installation counter it does not reset by default, a hunt pivot, and Huntback's exposed console shows a Global Administrator takeover at a South Korean university.

items.headline: PolinRider: forged backdated commits, npm hijacks and a fake recruiter run a loader at build or folder open
items.summary: Apiiro found the PolinRider loader in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories owned by 2,330 accounts, where stolen GitHub access force-pushes a copy of the owner's own commit, with the same author, message and date, plus a loader hidden after hundreds of spaces in a build configuration file. items.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and 8.6.0 on 2026-11-19 with fixes for up to 18 CVEs per branch. items.headline: Oracle CSPU: 56 unauthenticated rows at CVSS 9.0+, six at 10.0 in Access Manager, WebLogic, BI; Brotli rows on KEV
items.summary: Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update of 2026-11-17 carries 655 patches, and its risk matrices mark 56 of the 62 rows scoring CVSS 3.1 9.0 or above as remotely exploitable without authentication. Six are CVSS 10.0 with changed scope, in Oracle Access Manager (three rows), WebLogic Server TopLink Integration, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition, and WebLogic Server and E-Business Suite carry further unauthenticated rows at 9.8. The only exploited flaw among them is the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497, which CISA has listed as exploited since 2026-10-27 and which fills three of the unauthenticated rows; for attacks that need no privileges Oracle's interim measure is blocking the network protocols an attack needs.

items.headline: Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI carried a Python-startup stealer in 1.26.1 and 1.26.2; hash-lock the tree at 1.26.0
items.summary: Socket and SafeDep report that versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's official agent-framework metapackage were published to PyPI on 2026-11-17, about 33 minutes apart, with a .pth file that runs a credential stealer whenever Python starts, so a pip install in a CI job is enough. It collects environment secrets and credential files and requests Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and, in 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. Both versions were removed from PyPI and 1.26.0 is the last clean release; a second maintainer account created on the day of the attack can still publish agent-framework and five sibling projects, four of which 1.26.0 installs, and how it got access is not known.

items.headline: ESET: Turla's Cereal runs the victim's own Exchange server as C2 and wraps transport agents to collect mail
items.summary: ESET found a previously undocumented .NET toolset, Cereal, on a Kazakh government organisation's Exchange server in November 2025 and on a Romanian government organisation's from December 2025, and attributes it to Turla with high confidence. The compromised Exchange server is the command channel, answering requests on web paths that imitate Outlook Web Access, Autodiscover and ActiveSync, and a module injected into the transport service wraps existing transport agents to collect mail, in Romania configured to select messages to or from NATO and EU addresses; ESET could not determine the initial access method.

actions: Audit every FortiGate and SonicWall VPN gateway for VPN accounts with default or guessed passwords (guest, admin, test) or passwords that appear in credential dumps, reset or remove them, and search VPN logs since May 2026 for logins by such accounts that are followed by a broad LDAP enumeration from the VPN address pool, because Cyderes found a broker's toolkit and logs showing root-level tunnels into multiple victims.
items.headline: Cyderes: 'tcherber' VPN toolkit for FortiGate and SonicWall, credential file mixing default and real logins, LDAP sweep
items.summary: Cyderes' Howler Cell recovered a Go toolkit that wraps OpenConnect for FortiGate and NetExtender for SonicWall, a credential file of more than 500 FortiGate entries mixing default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords, and VPN connection logs showing sustained root-level tunnels into multiple victim environments in May and June 2026. Once the tunnel is up the orchestrator maps internal routes and enumerates Active Directory over LDAP, while port scanning, SMB reconnaissance and credential validation are manual tools. Cyderes assesses a Russian-speaking initial access broker and malware-as-a-service seller and names no victim, vulnerability or firmware version.

actions: On every host that runs CyberPower PowerPanel Business, domain controllers first, compare the extcmd and temp\\profile\\extcmd folders with the product defaults and compare the extcmd folders and the console's event-to-command assignments with what administrators configured and treat unknown scripts as hostile; where the techniques Symantec lists are found (ntdsutil or esentutl on a domain controller, scripts staged under extcmd that no administrator configured, a side-loaded implant), assume Active Directory credentials are exposed and plan a krbtgt reset and wider credential rotation, because Symantec saw this channel used to export ntds.dit from a domain controller.
items.headline: Symantec: attacker ran SYSTEM commands on a domain controller through CyberPower PowerPanel Business, then took ntds.dit
items.summary: Symantec analysed an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business, UPS-management software, as an execution channel on a Windows domain controller: scripts placed in the product's extcmd folder run through the ppbed.exe service as SYSTEM, and the operator iterated scripts until ntds.dit was exported with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss, then side-loaded an implant. Symantec does not say how the attacker reached the console (public advisories or stolen administrator credentials could give that access) and names no actor.

items.summary: Mandiant published CVE-2026-131914 on 2026-11-18 for Idunno.AntiCsrf, an open-source anti-CSRF HTTP module for ASP.NET WebForms last released in December 2008: any anonymously reachable page that does not opt out passes a crafted CSRF form field to an unvalidated deserializer, so one POST runs code in the IIS worker process (CVSS 4.0 9.3). Mandiant states that exploitation in the wild has been observed, names no actor, and says the project has no active maintainer or official patch, so the fix is to remove the module, and Mandiant adds that environments with evidence of exploitation should rotate the secrets held in the web configuration and inspect the web root.

items.headline: Barracuda: an unretired vendor cloud key led an ARTEX-consistent intruder across ten accounts in 44 hours
items.summary: Barracuda says an attacker used a valid cloud access key that it had issued to an AI-sector vendor for a past project and never retired, between 2026-11-01 04:33 and 2026-11-02 23:31 UTC, reading stored secrets and moving through about ten cloud accounts, a data analytics system, a source-code token and Kubernetes clusters. items.headline: Mandiant: COLD RELIC turns one cloud compromise into the pretext for the next; enrolled passkeys outlive password resets
items.summary: Mandiant reports that COLD RELIC, the name Google Threat Intelligence Group now uses for the group formerly tracked as COLDRIVER and UNC4057 (Star Blizzard), reused the staff directory and identities stolen from one US organisation in late 2025 to impersonate a contact when approaching a second in 2026. In the late-2025 case it took over a Super Admin account through push-notification fatigue, kept access with enrolled passkeys, MFA backup codes and rogue MFA devices that survived password and session resets, and exported the whole tenant; in 2026 it phished Entra ID credentials and registered a new MFA device to download one user's drive. GTIG names government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America as targets and says new phishing operations continued into November 2026.

items.summary: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were so weak that anyone could recover them and forge trusted HTTPS certificates for any site, and eMudhra's incident report of 2026-11-10 adds eight RSA intermediates revoked on 2026-11-07 because it cannot show their keys were handled as its policy requires. items.headline: Insikt: GhostFrame implant re-disables ESXi execInstalledOnly every five seconds and steals guest credentials
items.summary: Recorded Future's Insikt Group describes GhostFrame, a command-and-control and post-exploitation framework for VMware ESXi hosts that operators must already hold root on: its vmhostd-core implant persists through ESXi boot scripts, disables the ESXi firewall and the execInstalledOnly control about every five seconds, and a web panel controls guest VMs and runs VMkatz against memory snapshots and virtual disks to recover Windows credentials. Insikt links it to TAG-218, whose activity overlaps Settra ransomware and whose servers targeted SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet VPN appliances in the US and Europe from late August to October 2026.

items.summary: The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15, a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path that dates to Linux 4.4 and is reached by a SYN packet carrying IP options; the CNA scores it CVSS 9.8. Anthropic reports that Claude wrote an exploit giving a remote, unauthenticated attacker root on servers with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener, which CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce; the Go team says the bug is not specific to MPTCP and Akamai that disabling MPTCP does not prevent exploitation, and no source reports attacks. Citrix rates its XenServer 8.4 and 9 bulletin Critical and names fixes for Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager, XCP-ng released a kernel fix, MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 list the CVE, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ and Amazon Linux kernels are fixed, Ubuntu has fixed its generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10 while 20.04 and older and some HWE, FIPS, NVIDIA and Azure variant kernels were still in progress on 2026-11-10, and Sophos has shipped a Firewall hotfix and SD-RED firmware, while WatchGuard (Fireware OS, AP, Dimension) and Fortinet list their products as unresolved or under investigation without a fixed build, Fortinet offering an IPS virtual patch.

On each such host that allowed password logins while reachable, search the sshd log for an accepted password on an account whose password field is *, and check root's and the default alpine user's authorized_keys for keys nobody added and the init scripts for a service nobody installed, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited and GreyNoise saw both persistence steps.

items.headline: CISA lists the OpenSSH musl password bypass as exploited; update to 10.6p2 or turn passwords off
items.summary: OpenSSH Portable 10.6p2 of 2026-11-05 works around CVE-2026-123158, a password-authentication bypass on Linux systems that use musl libc and run sshd without PAM, Alpine's default OpenSSH server and OpenWrt among them: a password of 257 to 1,024 bytes logs in to an account whose password field is *. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory the same day and has rated the flaw actively exploited since 2026-11-10; Alpine shipped fixed packages for every branch back to 3.16. CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-09, and GreyNoise records hands-on logins on its gridpoints from 2026-11-07 that ended in a dropped Python implant; SANS ISC's sensors record attempts from 2026-11-05 and Previdian's from 2026-11-06, QNAP says its NAS systems are not affected, and no source reports a compromised production host.

actions: On every self-hosted ScreenConnect server your organisation or its IT providers run, list guest sessions with an exchange-and-role name or empty company or site fields, copy App_Data\\Session.db and its WAL file before deleting any, and where a technician connected to one from a client older than 26.6.5, inspect that workstation's ScreenConnect Temp and Startup folders and process history and treat text sent through the session as exposed credentials, because Huntress suspects the sessions are bait for the file-transfer flaw CVE-2026-84869.
items.headline: Huntress: 2,223 crypto-named fake sessions sit on 118 ScreenConnect servers, likely bait for unpatched technicians
items.summary: Huntress counted 2,223 unauthorized guest sessions on 118 self-hosted ScreenConnect servers at 109 MSP and organisation accounts, enrolled between 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-13 and named after crypto exchanges; on the 29 servers with complete history an operator revisited every 151 seconds to keep them online. Huntress's leading hypothesis, which it has not observed, is that they are bait for a technician with a client older than 26.6.5 to connect, so that CVE-2026-84869 runs a file on the technician's workstation; it saw no malicious activity from the sessions and found no overlap with the SCKit indicators.

actions: On every developer endpoint that runs Cursor, check extension-install telemetry for Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 installed between 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29; where it is found, isolate the host, remove the unauthorized SSH key, the persistence and any running tunnel process, because uninstalling the extension removes none of them, and rotate every credential reachable from the host from a trusted system.

Ask the admin of every Cursor team your organisation uses whether Cursor's email listing exposed keys arrived, and rotate every key it lists, because Cursor says coding-agent traces from sessions outside Privacy Mode held unredacted credentials.
items.headline: Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor
items.summary: Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension; coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor says the attacker could not log in there. Cursor's report of 2026-11-13 says the chain began with an access key it had issued to its vendor Fireworks AI, exposed by Fireworks, which gave the attacker a storage bucket of coding-agent traces holding some unredacted credentials, and that a stolen credential from the exposed data let the attacker write the extension straight onto the marketplace cache; Cursor says this was not a vulnerability in Anthropic's product.
